title: Intel® SHMEM: GPU-initiated OpenSHMEM using SYCL
problem: Communication libraries lack support for GPU-initiated operations where OpenSHMEM-style calls execute directly within GPU kernels on heterogeneous systems with GPUs and accelerators.
motivation: Modern HPC and AI applications on heterogeneous platforms require overlapping communications and computation on GPUs to achieve increased efficiency and performance.
method: Intel SHMEM puts OpenSHMEM-style communication functions (a standard way for different parts of a system to send messages to each other) directly into GPU kernels using SYCL (a programming framework for writing code that runs on graphics processors). This means GPUs can initiate their own communication without needing the main CPU to coordinate. The system automatically picks the best method for moving data based on what's available: either reading and writing memory directly from the GPU, or using a GPU copy engine (specialized hardware that transfers data). They also added extensions that let multiple threads running on the same GPU collaborate on communication operations.
key_novelty: GPU kernels can now directly call OpenSHMEM communication functions using SYCL, with extensions that enable multiple GPU threads to collaborate.
contributions: Intel SHMEM library enabling GPU-aware API calls supporting GPU memory operations
GPU-initiated communication operations embedded within GPU kernels using SYCL
Thread-collaborative extensions to the OpenSHMEM standard for GPU exploitation
Adaptive optimization selecting between direct load/store and GPU copy engine transfers
